The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00406

This kind of existence has both continuity and stability, and renewal and passing away. To continue, it needs an agent that sustains it; to come to be and pass away, it needs something that can receive it. It is therefore bodily or belongs to a body. It also has one continuous identity and many renewed stages. As one thing, it must have one agent and one recipient. A single attribute cannot belong to one subject through many agents. Its agent must be free of matter and its ties; otherwise, the agent would need another motion and another time to undergo its own material changes.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00407

Its recipient must be the oldest and most complete of natural substances and bodies, since only time itself can precede time in this special sense. It cannot be formed from another body, or another body formed from it, because that would break time's continuity. It must be fully formed, not made from the elements, and by nature it cannot undergo change of place, change of amount such as growth or shrinking, expansion or contraction, or change of quality. These changes would break it and would mean it no longer came before the other bodies. We will explain this more simply as we continue.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00408
XXXI. Gradual Existence as the Immediate Goal of Time and Motion
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00409

You should know that we will show later that the proper goal of the celestial motion is the soul's conceptions, which give rise to longing and will. Through these, the celestial soul draws closer to its highest source.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00410

In his Notes, Avicenna writes: “The goal of celestial motion is not motion itself, simply as this particular motion. It is to preserve the nature of motion.” But the individual motion cannot be preserved, so the kind is preserved through individuals, just as the human kind survives only through individual people. One person cannot preserve it alone: every individual comes to be and must therefore pass away. Celestial motion is renewed, yet it is one motion through its continuity and permanence. In that respect, and when viewed as a whole, it is like something fixed.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00411

Elsewhere he writes: “The goal of a particular nature is a particular individual, such as the individual that comes to be after it. That individual can also be the goal of another particular nature. The endless succession of individuals is the goal of the lasting power within the heavenly substances.”
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00412

He also writes: “The cause of the sphere's motion is the soul's conception, renewed from one conception to the next. Each conception, together with a particular position, gives rise to another conception. The first prepares the soul for the second. Repeated conceptions may be alike in kind but many in number, or they may differ from one another.”
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00413

He adds: “The second conception resembles the first in kind, not as the same individual. It can therefore give rise to a motion like the first in kind, but not the same motion as an individual. If the two conceptions were identical in every way, there would be only one conception and one numerically single motion.” And he says: “Every position of the sphere calls for another position; the cause is the renewal of one perception after another.” These are his exact words. In effect, they affirm motion in substantial forms in two ways.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00414

First, the celestial soul's conceptions are renewed in a gradual, continuous way. That is what motion in a substantial form means. Avicenna and others have established that the form of a substance is itself a substance. The sphere's conceptions belong both to the principles that move it directly and to things that follow from those principles indirectly. They also hold that the sphere's goal is not anything below it. Its purposes and imaginings, then, are substantial forms nobler than the earthly substances.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00415

Second, a body's position is either part of its way of existing or inseparable from it, as they themselves have said. Every position of the sphere is natural to it; none is forced, since nothing can force the celestial bodies. You have already learned that the immediate source of every motion is nature. In truth, the sphere's nature and its animal soul are one thing, one reality. A change of position therefore means a change in the individual way the sphere exists: one individual existence follows another, continuously and gradually.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00416

Avicenna also says in his Notes: “The celestial nature, precisely as celestial nature, requires its natural place and position, but not one particular place.” Otherwise, moving away from that place would be forced.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00417

He also says: “All these positions and places are natural to it.” I say: this means every position and place of the sphere is natural to it. Yet it moves from one to another while each is natural. This makes sense only if the sphere's nature is itself renewed, with a shared unity and a connected multiplicity, along with the positions, places, and other features that follow from it. Avicenna and his followers may not accept this view, but it is the truth that cannot be avoided.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00418

What best fits their own account is that the celestial nature first requires position and place in general, without requiring any particular one. The particular positions and places serve only to preserve the kind indirectly, not as the nature's own goal. But this does not hold up under closer examination. First, they have established that nature's goal must be a particular individual. A general meaning has no existence outside the mind until it is made particular. Existence belongs first to the individual, then to the kind, and then to the general class. That is why, in Aristotle's Categories, primary substances are called first substances, their kinds second substances, and their general classes third substances.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00419

Second, as we have learned in the study of existence, what truly exists in any thing is its particular reality of existence, made individual through itself. General natures, by contrast, have no existence outside or inside the mind apart from their dependence on an existing thing. Position and place are among the features that make an existence particular and among the things that follow from it. A change in them is either the very change in the thing's way of existing or follows from it. It is not true, as people commonly think, that this body, as one fixed individual, is the unrestricted cause of time. If it were, it would not itself be in time. But every body and bodily thing is in time and is made particular by time; the cause of something cannot itself be made particular by that thing.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00420

Time, through its continuous unity, relates equally to all its earlier and later parts. It brings about time and the things in time through one act, and the source of their beginning is also the source of their continuing existence. A gradual thing that has no fixed state survives only by continually coming to be. As our approach shows, every body, bodily nature, and bodily feature—shape, position, amount, quality, place, and the other material features—is always flowing and passing away, either in itself or through something else.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00421

The unrestricted source of time must therefore have two aspects: a unifying, intellectual aspect and a renewing, changing aspect. Through its unity, it brings about time as one connected reality. Through its renewal, it is affected at one point and acts at another, according to the particular identities of its parts. This source is the outermost sphere itself, which has two sides: its separate, intellectual nature is the side of unity, and its bodily nature is the side of multiplicity and renewal. The outermost body brings time into being, sustains it, and keeps it going.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00422

By the same reasoning, its body also brings into being directions and places. A particular body needs time and motion for its capacity to change and for its gradual coming-to-be. In the same way, it needs something around it to establish its place and position. How, then, could place and position come before it by nature? These features either help make an individual what it is or necessarily follow from its existence. No act can be inserted between a thing and what necessarily follows from it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00423

All bodily existences are incomplete: they need time and place, position, amount, and quality. The first source of these things must therefore be separate from them in its being and existence. Time cannot be caused by an earlier time, place by an earlier place, or position by another position, and the same is true of amount and the rest. These things are renewed effects, but their first cause must be a stable, immaterial reality outside the chain of time and place: God in His oneness, or His divine knowledge, His perfect words that never fade, or the realm of His command, where when He says “Be,” it is.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00424
XXXII. Nothing Precedes Time and Motion Except God, Exalted in Glory
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00425

You have learned that time and the things connected with it are gradual existences, continually coming to be. Anything that precedes time—whether it is an existence, a nonexistence, or something else—if its “before” cannot coexist with what comes after, must itself be time or something in time. So before every time there would be another time, and before every motion another motion.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00426

We have also established that a thing's cause must not depend in its own existence on the thing it causes. Therefore, nothing precedes time except God, His power and command. Different thinkers have called this command God's detailed knowledge, His attributes, the angels, or the divine forms known to the Platonists. People follow different paths according to what they love.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00427

If anything else preceded time and motion through a succession of renewed states, then, when it existed, time and motion would not yet exist. Before they existed, they would have been possible. If they had not been possible, they would have had to be either necessary or impossible, and either would require reality to reverse: what had been absent would become present. That is impossible. But the possibility of motion must belong to something capable of motion, as we have shown. That can only be a body or something bodily. Whenever a thing capable of motion does not move, either its moving cause is absent or some condition of that cause is missing. When motion begins, a moving cause or one of its conditions must have come to be. The same question then arises about the coming-to-be of that cause, and the question continues without end.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00428

A chain of causes arranged in order cannot all exist together, and a chain of causes coming one after another cannot consist of separate, disconnected moments. Both are impossible, as we have shown and as the leading philosophers agree. If causes existed one by one, each in an instant that immediately followed the last, there would be instants with no time between them. The impossibility of this will be explained when we discuss indivisible atoms and what follows from them. If, instead, each cause existed in a different time, with gaps between those times, then neither the causes nor their times would exist in reality or even in the mind. Things that do not exist in either way cannot stand in an ordered or causal relation to one another. Time exists as one connected individual reality, not as separate pieces. We cannot imagine an infinite number of separate times and temporal things either; such an imagined series would not match what exists.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00429

If the causes are connected and continuous, each arising after the last, then the reality that is itself connected and renewed is the existence of substantial nature: the form of a body, with the body's capacity as its matter. Its continuity is motion in the sense of a connected path, and the measure of that continuity is time. Its lasting root is always the middle between its limits and parts. In one respect those parts are also parts of the nature itself. The flowing instant corresponds to this lasting middle, just as the middle stage of motion corresponds to the whole connected path.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00430

Here, then, is one intellectual reality that acts through endlessly many states, as the Qur'an says: “Every day He is at work.” This reality cannot be a body or anything bodily. Anything bodily is subject to time and motion. The source must therefore be a soul, an intellect, or God Himself. It cannot be a soul insofar as the soul is attached to a body: in that respect, it is like material nature and a changing bodily form. The independent source of time and all the renewed things in time must be God Himself, or His highest command, called the Active Intellect or the Spirit. This is a near angel containing many angels who serve God, as the Qur'an says: “None knows the hosts of your Lord but He.”
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00431

The Spirit's relation to God is like the relation of a command to the one who gives it, or of speech to the speaker. God is the source of both command and creation. The created world includes whatever has form, measure, and dimensions: bodies and bodily things. These come to be gradually, their identities following in succession, through God's power and knowledge. The realm of command is different: God has always acted, known, and willed, and He has always issued His command. His command is eternal, while what He creates comes to be. That is why scripture says, “God's command is done,” not “God's creation is done.”
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00432
XXXIII. How the Changing Is Linked to the Eternal
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00433

The minds of theologians and philosophers have long been troubled by the question of how what comes to be can depend on the eternal. The strongest and most reasonable of their answers is this: all changing things depend on a lasting, circular motion. This motion needs no cause that begins in time, because it has no beginning in time. In one respect it is eternal and depends on an eternal cause; in another respect it is always coming to be and is the source of changing things.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00434

If someone asks how its changing aspect can need no changing cause, when we have said as a general rule that every thing that comes to be needs a cause that also comes to be, we answer: the subject of that rule is an essence that has coming-to-be as a feature. Circular motion is different. Its very essence is coming-to-be and renewal.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00435

If that renewal belongs to it by its very nature, it does not need a cause that is itself renewed. When we reflect on the matter, we find that we judge a cause must come to be only when its effect comes to be while the effect's essence is not renewal itself. We do not make that judgment about an effect that is nothing but renewal and change, unless a further change is added to it—for example, a motion that begins after it did not exist. That is different from a continuous motion that never stops. Nor does the cause required by a changing effect need to undergo an additional change; otherwise, changing things could not depend on continuous motion.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00436

In short, every change ends in something whose very nature is change and passing away. Since it is always coming to be, its cause need not itself begin in time. And since it is change itself, it can be the cause of changing things. This is why some define motion as a state that, by its very nature, cannot remain fixed.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00437

I say: this account does remove many difficulties, but it still contains serious flaws. First, motion is a relation. In itself it is neither beginningless nor newly begun; it takes on these features through what it is related to. As we have already said, motion means that something moves from potentiality to actuality little by little. Strictly speaking, the thing that changes is what moves from potentiality to actuality; motion is the renewal of what changes, the coming-to-be of what comes to be.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00438

Second, motion exists only as potentiality. It cannot precede something that has already come to be in actuality. We are discussing a cause that brings a thing into existence. Such a cause must exist together with what it causes, while being prior to it in the order of nature. A thing that has come to be therefore needs a cause that also comes to be, exists with it in time, comes before it in the order of nature, and has a stronger way of existing than it. But motion is not actual in this way.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00439

Third, the other thinker's argument treats circular motion as eternal in one respect, and says that in that respect it depends on an eternal cause. That is not right. Pure renewal has no lasting existence at all, let alone an eternal one. A universal essence, meanwhile, is not made by a cause; it does not make anything either. Its continuity is no proof.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00440

Fourth, we have proved that neither the sphere's substantial form, its natural position, nor the celestial bodies and stars remain the same individual through time. The cause and subject of motion is an individual body, which is not eternal. So it is wrong to say that motion has an eternal cause; it is also wrong to say that it needs no cause that comes to be.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00441

The true view is this: what is renewed in its own being and identity is the existence of bodily nature. It has a reality in God's knowledge and a connected, gradual identity in prime matter, which is pure potentiality and readiness. The nature's essence is not “coming-to-be,” but its way of existing is renewal and coming-to-be. This is like the difference between a substance's essence, which the mind can consider apart from a subject, and its actual existence in the world, where it depends on a subject. Existence can have features that an essence considered apart from existence does not have. As the existence of different things varies in strength and weakness while their essences do not, so some existences are gradual in their identity, not because of a separate feature added to them. Their very way of existing is gradual, though their essence is not.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00442
The existence of bodily nature, which gives form to material bodies, is too limited to remain as one individual forever. It can exist only as a gradual succession.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00443

I do not mean that the essence of a bodily nature requires change and passing away when considered apart from existence. We can think of a bodily nature without thinking of it as changing, just as we can think of it without thinking of it as lasting. How, then, could change be one of its essential or defining features? The mistake lies in confusing the essence of a thing with its existence. Existence itself cannot be pictured in the mind, as we have explained many times. It is made individual through itself, while everything in the mind is open to sharing and generalization. If existence could be represented in the mind, an individual would become general, what is outside the mind would become something mental, and existence would become an essence. All of this is impossible.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00444
1. A Clarifying Note
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00445

Many things do not have an intellectual reality that matches the way they appear to the senses or imagination. This is true of time, motion, a circle, and power. It is also true of quantities and mathematical objects, such as a body considered simply as an extended quantity. Its mode of existence consists in a particular spatial extension, whether it exists in matter and a specific natural body or in the imagination apart from any specific matter and nature. It has no existence in the intellect as an extended thing, because anything understood by the intellect is general; a general idea cannot itself be extended or measured, nor can it exist as something extended and measured. The intellectual idea of quantity is not itself a quantity, nor is it something with quantity, nor can it be treated as quantity in the ordinary way.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00446

Many material things are like this: there is no intellectual counterpart that matches them exactly as they exist. In fact, if you ask me what is true, none of the particular forms of actual bodily things, simple or compound, has an exact match in the intellect. They are individual realities that cannot be shared, while what the intellect grasps is general and can be shared. The same is true of the gradual, changing forms of bodily nature. The specific forms that distinguish bodily kinds and ground their defining features are, in truth, renewed existences. Taken as fleeting instants, they have no essence of their own. The mind does draw general ideas from them and calls these ideas essences. In reality, those ideas follow from the existences, though they are essential to the meanings drawn from them.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00447

We will prove in this book that the specific forms of substances do not fall under the general category of substance, or under any category of qualities. They are individual realities of existence that do not, in their own right, belong to substance, quantity, quality, or any other category or class. They are pure existences flowing from the aspects of the First Reality, effects of its intellectual rays and shadows of its light.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00448
2. Discussion and Clarification
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00449

You can put the objection this way: how can these renewed realities, called specific forms and bodily natures, come from an eternal source? If they come from it without a prepared recipient, then they must be separate forms, and so intellectual rather than material. Besides being impossible, this contradicts what we are trying to explain: renewal is incompatible with a separate, immaterial existence.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00450

If they come from an eternal source through a prepared recipient, then if the recipient is itself new, it must depend on another recipient and a prior readiness, and so on without end. If the recipient is eternal, either it is sufficient by itself to receive the form or it is sufficient together with something that necessarily follows from it. In either case, the form would also be fixed, not renewed, even though we assumed it was renewed.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00451

If the recipient is not sufficient by itself, nor with anything that necessarily follows from it, to receive the form, and instead needs later, changing preparations, then you must accept that matter is eternal and that an endless succession of events follows. But you are trying to prove that the world and everything in it began in time. You would also have to accept that there is one eternal matter for each specific form and kind, so that the number of eternal individuals would match the number of specific forms. In any case, the argument returns to the coming-to-be of each particular readiness. Potentiality depends on actuality; each specific readiness comes to be through an actual form that precedes it by nature, though not in time, because that form is its essential cause rather than a mere preparation.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00452

I reply that what I have said already resolves this problem and similar ones. If the receptive matter is prime matter, its unity is a unity of kind, not a single numerical identity. Prime matter means substance in potentiality; being a substance does not give it a specific form. Potentiality is a lack of actuality, and it becomes actual only through whatever form it receives. If the matter is some other kind of matter, the same account applies insofar as it is matter: its potentiality and incompleteness have one source.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00453

Any other matter becomes actual through the form paired with it, though it is more actual than prime matter because it has already been made actual once. Each form through which matter becomes actual is prior to that matter in its basic reality. But as an individual form in matter, it is one with that matter; the two are individual together and take on their limits together. I do not mean that the form is one with matter through some prior readiness: that readiness is set against the form and is not one with it. Rather, each readiness of a later individual of a nature may imply an earlier individual, prior to it in time, but the readiness itself is prior in the order of nature. You have already seen how renewed realities that are passing away work this way. In short, nothing here requires any matter to be eternal.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00454

I have also indicated that every bodily nature has a reality with God, present in His knowledge. In that intellectual reality, it needs no matter, readiness, motion, time, nonexistence, coming-to-be, or potentiality. But it has successive, worldly states of existence connected continuously. Their continuous unity depends on the unity of the nature present in God's knowledge. If you consider these states as many, each appears at a particular time. In that respect, it needs a receptive matter prepared for it earlier in time. As potentiality, that recipient is something lacking in actuality and does not need a specific cause; it needs only some form, whatever form that may be. It may be the power belonging to a form that is clothed in potentiality, or the potentiality that belongs to a form, or the potentiality for some further perfection. But the recipient's particular, immediate readiness does require a particular form: that form gives it the capacity for a certain kind of change and a certain form.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00455

When the recipient leaves one specific, immediate potentiality for the actuality opposed to it, that potentiality disappears. The earlier form gives way to the later form because the two cannot exist together. The form of an embryo, for example, disappears when the form of the animal comes to be; the embryo-form was potentiality and a possibility for the animal-form. Every new form arises with the passing away of the previous one, then passes away in turn as its successor comes to be. This happens continuously through renewal.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00456

Why does each particular form belong to its particular time? Sometimes nothing beyond that form's own individual reality explains the timing. This is so when it has a continuous identity that does not break between what comes before and after; in that case, no further cause is needed to place it at that time. If the individuals of a nature are disconnected from each other, the question does arise. Then some further cause makes each reality belong to its particular time. That cause must exist at the time in question. This continues until the causes reach a particular reality whose own identity makes it belong to that time, without a further cause. The chain cannot continue without end among causes that each require another cause.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00457

Existence differs in its basic reality from one kind of thing to another. God, an angel, a devil, a human being, fire, and water each have a reality and a rank of their own. They do not share one kind of existence. This is one way existences differ. They can also differ through additional features, even when their underlying kind is the same: the existence of Zayd differs from that of ʿAmr, and individual horses differ in the same way. Shades of blackness or whiteness may also differ in strength while occupying the same level of their quality. So a human being differs from a horse, and black from white, through the basic reality of each; but individuals of the same kind differ through additional, individuating features.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00458

Sometimes, however, a reality that differs through itself, not because a separate maker has made it different, is made by one simple act into a single identity with many changing states. Those states differ through their own earlier and later order, with no separate before or after added to them. The connected time of the common account is like this: they say time has one identity whose parts differ in earlier and later position. Our account of bodily nature is similar, except that its identity is substantial while time, on their view, is an accident. In truth, the substantial form of nature is what has these features in itself, not time. For them, time is an accident whose existence depends on what it measures. Time is the measure of nature's renewal through its own earlier and later states, just as mathematical body measures nature's three dimensions. Nature therefore has two extensions and two measures: a gradual, temporal extension, divisible in thought into earlier and later times; and a fixed, spatial extension, divisible into earlier and later places. A measure relates to its extension as a definite limit to something indefinite; they are one in existence but distinct in how we consider them.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00459

Just as mathematical extension in matter cannot be separate from the spatial extension it measures, time cannot be separate from the gradual extension of what renews itself. Time's relation to natural form, which has temporal extension, is like mathematical quantity's relation to bodily form, which has spatial extension. Keep this point in mind: it is more useful than many scattered arguments. A little reflection on time shows that it exists only in the mind as an aspect of what it measures. It does not exist as a separate feature attached to its subject in the way that color or heat does. Time is an analytical feature of what it measures. It exists outside the mind only through the existence of what it measures, because the distinction between time and what it measures is made only in thought.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00460

Since time exists in the world only through the existence of what it measures, its renewal, passing away, coming-to-be, and continuity depend on that thing's own renewal, passing away, coming-to-be, and continuity. It is surprising that some philosophers still assign time an independently renewed identity. Perhaps they mean that motion is, by nature, the renewal and passing away of something, while time is the quantity of that motion. That is why the author of Pointers thought motion, considered as measurable, was the same as time, though motion as motion was different. In the world, motion and time do not differ; they differ only in the mind, when we consider motion without considering its measure.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00461
3. Discussion continued
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00462

In The Healing, Avicenna says people have held several views about time. Some deny that it exists at all. Some say it exists only as something imagined, with no real existence. Others say it is not one thing in itself, but a relation between various events and other events, each of which serves as the time of another. On that view, time is the sum of such occasions.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00463

Some treat time as one independent substance separate from bodies. Others say time is a bodily substance, the outermost sphere itself. Others identify it with motion. Some say that only the sphere's motion is time, and still others say that time is one full revolution of the sphere.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00464

These were the views known in earlier times, listed in the study of nature. Abu al-Barakat of Baghdad held that time is the measure of existence. The Ashʿarite theologians adopted the third view. Some who held the fourth view imagined time to be a separate, self-subsisting existence, even necessary in itself. Some early philosophers also described it as a separate substance, distinct from matter, and ascribed this view to the divine Plato and his followers.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00465

The starting point for both groups was that no change occurs in time's own reality or duration. If no motion or change took place in time, they thought, it would contain only permanence and eternity, though it could still be called earlier or later because of its relation to changing things. If related to beings that last and do not change, time in that respect is called eternity. If related to things that move and change, it is called the everlasting age. If related to changes that occur within it, it is called time.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00466

In Eastern Investigations, after listing the different views and objections, the author admits: “I have not yet reached the true nature of time. Let this book satisfy you by examining what can be said from every side. I will not twist the answers to favor one group over another, especially on this question.”
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00467

In his commentary on ʿUyūn al-Ḥikma, after setting out the views and objections, he says that defenders of Aristotle's account of time as the measure of motion cannot enter the most difficult questions about time without returning to Plato's view. He himself finds Plato's view most convincing: time exists by itself, independent of other things. He then describes the three relations just mentioned, which are called eternity, the everlasting age, and time.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00468

He adds that Plato's view is closer to sound proof and farther from the darkness of doubt, though perfect knowledge comes only from God. He also argues that common sense says the God of the world existed before today's event, exists with it now, and will remain after it. If earlier, present, and later states implied change in the thing described by them, then the Necessary Being would change, which no reasonable person accepts. If someone answers that God could not be called prior, present, and later without change in the event, he replies that they already allow a thing to be described as prior, present, and later because something else changes. Why, then, could time not be that way too?
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00469

Plato, he says, held that when no motion or change occurs, time contains only permanence and continuity, which is called the everlasting age or eternity. When motion and change occur in it, earlier and later arise—not because time itself changes, but because other things do. That is his account.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00470

I say: you have learned by decisive proof that there is a reality whose very existence is renewed and passing away, with no separate act that first gives it existence and then gives it renewal. By God's grace, when we come to the proper place in this book, the difficulties that made time and motion seem so hard to understand will be resolved. The First Reality is too exalted to be earlier or later than daily events in a temporal sense, or to exist at the same time as them in the ordinary way. His presence with them is a sustaining presence, beyond time, motion, change, and coming-to-be. Perhaps those who deny that time exists at all mean only that it has no existence apart from the existence of what renews itself. Those who deny that time exists outside the mind may mean that it is an analytical feature, added to an essence in thought, not an independently existing feature added to its subject in reality.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00471

Those who call time a bodily substance and identify it with the outermost sphere may mean the sphere's renewed nature. In that case, they mean by “sphere” its nature itself. This agrees with our view that time measures nature according to its own renewal. We have also indicated that time, like mathematical extension, is not an independently existing feature. The existence of a measure is first the existence of what it measures, and it is an “accident” only by analysis.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00472

Those who describe time as a separate substance may mean the separate intellectual reality of the natural form, whose material existence is measured and extended through renewal, while its existence in God's knowledge is fixed and eternal. And those who say that time is necessary in itself may mean something higher than people understand.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00473

A prophetic saying tells us not to curse time, because time is God. People cursed time when misfortune came, imagining that time brought it about. The saying corrects them: God, not time, brings about events. It may also mean that time is God's effect and the record of His pen; whoever loves a thing loves its traces and its work. Or “time” may mean the realm of the universal intellects, which belongs to the divine order. In that sense, ordinary time is a subtle reflection of a higher reality.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00474

The sages also say: the relation of the fixed to the fixed is eternity; the relation of the fixed to the changing is the everlasting age; and the relation of the changing to the changing is time. By the first, they mean the relation of God to His names and knowledge. By the second, the relation of His fixed knowledge to its changing objects—the beings of the bodily world—as they exist together. By the third, the temporal relation of those objects to one another.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00475
XXXIV. Why Time Has No First or Last Moment
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00476

Some say that every event in time is preceded by a nonexistence that does not coexist with its existence. What makes that nonexistence “before” the event cannot be nonexistence itself, since nonexistence may also come after something. Nor can it be the event's cause: the cause also exists alongside its effect. And nothing that can exist together with the later event is, by its own nature, earlier than it in this particular way.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00477

So for nonexistence to be earlier, that nonexistence must be tied to a time, and the event's existence must begin in a later time. Then, before any moment chosen as the beginning of time, there must be another time, and the same argument applies to an ending. Time as a whole can have no beginning or end. As the Teacher of the Philosophers says, those who say time began have, without realizing it, also said that it has always existed. We have learned that time follows motion, and motion follows nature. Nature exists only in matter and body. God's generosity and giving never cease; His goodness has no end or limit. As scripture says, “If you tried to count God's blessings, you could not number them.” Even so, every particular time and motion, and every body, comes to be in time and is bounded by nonexistence on both sides, as we have explained. This is a strange conclusion.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00478

Someone may object that this “before” is only imagined, like the supposed emptiness beyond the world's limits. Just as the world ending in space does not require its nonexistence to occupy another place, time ending need not require its nonexistence to occupy another time. I reply that the mind plainly recognizes an order between a thing's existence and its nonexistence, since they cannot coexist. That order is not causal, since cause and effect must exist together. It is not natural priority either, since what is prior by nature may exist together with what is later by nature. It is plainly not priority of rank or place. It must therefore be priority in time. In short, this kind of order is what we mean by time. If there is no such order, then you have admitted that time did not come into existence after nonexistence. If there is such an order, then the nonexistence of time must itself be in time.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00479
The comparison with imagined places beyond the world fails. Space can be finite without needing another space beyond it. But for something to begin to exist, it must be preceded by nonexistence.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00480

If someone says this makes God subject to time, and requires another time for time, with an endless regress of times, I reply: the claim that God precedes a particular time also concerns time. Although God is beyond change and beyond time and the things that coexist in time, He is with every thing without physical contact or being mixed with it. He is with the earlier time in a way that does not change Him. We may therefore truly say He exists before a particular time, just as He exists with it and after it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00481

The claim that every time is preceded by another time, because the nonexistence of each time occurs in a time, means that before every time there is another time, before every motion another motion, and before every body another body, without beginning. This regress is not impossible. These things have a weak mode of existence in which existence and nonexistence are intertwined: the existence of one particular time entails the nonexistence of another, and the nonexistence of one entails the existence of another. Time's nonexistence occurs only in time.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00482

Someone may object that God's being present with a time requires another time in which God and that time are together. Likewise, if time's nonexistence is present with the preceding or following time, that seems to require another time. I reply: when two things are together in time and neither one is time itself, they need a time that contains them both. But the relation between time and something that exists in time does not require another time, because the time itself is what makes them present together. Each time is distinct through itself. It is one kind of existence that cannot be anything other than this particular time, before or after itself. The same applies to every other time and every part of time. Their existence in the form they have is made necessary by a simple act of creation. Therefore, the presence of a thing with a time does not require yet another time.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00483

When two things that are not themselves times exist together, their being together requires a third thing that makes them simultaneous. The same is true of priority and posteriority. Time has priority and posteriority by its own nature, since these belong to what time is. Each time is earlier than some times, later than others, and present with whatever coincides with it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00484

This does not mean that time belongs to the category of relation. That confuses the concept of a thing with its existence. The concept of time belongs to quantity: time is a continuous amount that does not remain fixed. What is understood from it may imply another concept, but its actual existence depends on another thing or its nonexistence. Priority and posteriority belong to time's essence because its existence is itself the existence of priority and posteriority. It is the concepts of priority and posteriority, not their existence as what makes things earlier or later, that belong to the category of relation.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00485

There is another difficulty: the parts of time must differ in essence, even though parts of a continuum must resemble one another. Each part of time has its own place in the order of earlier and later. Thursday cannot be Wednesday, nor can it be a different Thursday that comes before or after it. This seems to bring back the same impossibilities.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00486

The answer is that a continuous whole's parts resemble one another in what makes it continuous. Their differences are required by this very continuity. Each part of one stretch of space has a different position from the others, and the unity and continuity of space require this. The same is true of the hours of time: each has a different state, and the unity and continuity of time require it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00487
XXXV. Arguments for a Beginning of Time and Replies
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00488

Those who say time began offer several arguments. First, past events can increase or decrease in number. Whatever can increase or decrease must have a beginning, so past events must have had one. Second, if past events were infinite in number, the event happening today would depend on an infinite number of earlier events having passed away. It could not then happen. But it plainly does happen, so the past cannot be infinite. Third, if every individual event has a beginning, the whole collection must have a beginning too. Fourth, past events have reached us. If they were infinite, then an infinite series would have come to an end, which is a contradiction. Fifth, either an event occurred in eternity or none did. The first is impossible, since then the event would not be a new event. If no event occurred in eternity, there was a time when no event existed, so all events began after nonexistence.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00489

Sixth, past events have entered into existence. Whatever has entered into existence has thereby been bounded and counted, so past events must be finite. Seventh, suppose a body had existed eternally and that it contained events with no first event. That body would precede neither their existence nor their nonexistence, which is impossible.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00490
Eighth, the world is never without events, and whatever is never without events must itself have begun. So the world began.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00491

These arguments are weak when used to show that time and motion themselves began. The first argument is taken from the proof that spatial dimensions are finite. It can be stated this way: count the revolutions, years, or past souls, then add one more revolution, year, or soul from the future. The two totals differ by a finite amount. Compare them by matching their parts, and one must exceed the other by a finite amount. What exceeds something by a finite amount must itself be finite.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00492

But this reasoning applies to things that can exist together. Past motions, times, and events cannot all exist together. Any proof that depends on their being gathered into one whole cannot establish a limit for them. The past can be infinite precisely because its events are not all present at once. Their continuity depends on each later event coming after an earlier one, and the later existence of one is tied to the earlier nonexistence of another. So how could one make the impossible assumption that they exist all together, then use that assumption to rule out infinity? It uses a contradiction as the basis for its proof.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00493

The second argument also fails. What cannot depend on an infinite series is something whose existence waits on all the infinitely many things before it, none of which has yet come to be. Such a thing cannot happen. But this is not the situation with the past. There was never a time when an infinite series of past events was still waiting to occur, followed by the present event. If the claim is simply that no event occurs except after an infinite past, that is the very question under debate, not proof against it.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00494

The third argument wrongly transfers what is true of each individual to the whole. The objectors could make a stronger case by saying that the collection of past rational souls must itself have begun, since each soul in it began. Then, they argue, the collection too must have begun, since it is the result of those individual beginnings. This is a stronger argument than simply giving the whole the same property as each of its members: it tries to infer that an effect begins because its causes began. But it still does not prove their conclusion. The total collection of souls does not cause time and all the events within it. At every moment another collection exists, as more souls leave their bodies. The world as a whole is also renewed at every moment. Neither claim shows that the number of past events is finite.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00495

The fourth argument proves only that the past has an end on the side that reaches us. An end on one side does not rule out that it has no beginning on the other. The motions of the people of Paradise, for example, have no end, yet they had a beginning.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00496

The fifth argument assumes that eternity is a particular time with a definite state. It is not. Eternity means the absence of a first moment. A temporal event that is preceded by nonexistence cannot occur in eternity, but this objection can be turned around: was the possibility of events present in eternity or not? If it was present, then an event could have occurred eternally, which is impossible. If it was not present, that possibility must itself have begun, which is also impossible. This argument does not disprove the possibility of events; otherwise it would also disprove God's power to bring events about. The same reply applies here.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00497

The sixth argument assumes that to be bounded is to have two ends. We agree that past events have an end on the side that reaches us. But an end on one side does not rule out that events can continue without beginning on the other. And we can turn the argument around and ask whether events can begin at all.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00498

The seventh argument assumes either that one body is described at once by all past events and by their absence, or that at every time it is described by one event and by the absence of another. The first is false: the whole collection of past events does not exist at once, so the body is not described by all of them together. The second is not contradictory. At any given time, the body is described by one event and by the absence of different events; it is not both present and absent in the same respect.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00499

The eighth argument is close to the earlier arguments and, as usually stated, has flaws in its premises. If “the world” means all bodies, then it is never without motion and other changing features. If it means the world considered as one collection, then, as we have already explained, there is a new collection at each moment; that does not show there are only finitely many events. If “the world” means everything other than God, the premise is false, because some possible beings do not change at all.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00500

The second premise also has a problem. If “never without events” means that the world is never without any particular event, it is plainly false: the world precedes every particular event. If it means that the world is never without the entire collection of events, there is no such collection of all events for anything to precede. The claim that anything which does not precede all events must itself have begun simply assumes what it is trying to prove. On the opponent's own view, the heavenly bodies are never without motion and never precede it in time. To make their case, the objectors must return to the claim that past events are finite, which we have already answered.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00501

These are the arguments and replies that have passed between the two sides. With God's help, we have explained how the world began and how every particular body, nature, soul, and accident is preceded by temporal nonexistence. We have also shown that these claims can stand together: the world's substances are never without change, and whatever is never without change has itself begun in time. We have already established some of what is needed for this conclusion; the rest will be discussed in its proper place, God willing.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00502

Most people find it difficult to state their own view clearly or identify where the disagreement lies. If they say “the world began,” ask what they mean. If they mean that it depends on a Maker, their opponents agree completely. The philosophers say the world depends on a maker both when it begins and as it continues, in its essence and in its features. If they mean that a period of time came before the world, they cannot accept that: they consider everything other than God to be the world, and time is part of the world. How, then, could time come before the world?
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00503

If they say “the world is not eternal,” the philosophers agree that it is not eternal in the sense of being necessary in itself. If they mean that it is not lasting, ask what “lasting” means. In everyday speech it can mean that something exists for a long time. In that sense, there is no dispute that the world lasts. If they mean there was a time when the world did not exist, that conflicts with their view, since there was no time before the world—just as there cannot be a time before time. If they say the world is not beginningless, ask what “beginningless” means; the same difficulty returns.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00504

If they say that the number of past motions in the mind is finite, the philosophers agree: any number of motions held in the mind is finite. But that does not mean the world depends for its existence on anything other than God. Even if we imagine the past events together as one collection, that imagined collection has begun too. If they say the world was nonexistent and then came to be, then if “was” means “before it in time,” their claim contradicts itself and assumes that time existed before the world. If “was” means priority in the order of nature, the philosophers agree: they say the possible thing is nothing in itself and becomes something through its cause.
The fourth kind: Power that produces different actions with awareness
passage-en-00505

If someone says God preceded the world by a period of time, that is not the religious position. Before the world, they say, there was nothing but God's own being. The philosophers say the same. The real priority is the priority of a cause, the truest kind of priority. The disagreement is therefore not about time. It is whether the world depends on something other than God, as a partner in its existence, or whether God's own being and attributes are enough to bring it into existence. Once that is clear, we can distinguish belief in one God from treating another as His partner.
